explanation: The glycine-to-serine substitution introduces a bulky hydroxyl-bearing side chain (29 Å³ volume increase) into the sterically constrained NNRTI-binding pocket core, which directly contacts nevirapine at a minimum distance of 3.7 Å, creating steric clash that destabilizes the ligand's optimal binding geometry. Although the mutation adds a polar hydroxyl group, this gain in potential hydrogen bonding capacity is outweighed by the unfavorable van der Waals repulsion from the enlarged side chain, forcing nevirapine to adopt a suboptimal conformational state or partially escape the binding site. The net effect is a destabilization of approximately 0.6 kcal/mol, explaining the loss of binding affinity and emergence of phenotypic resistance.
